chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked, 'Which deed is the most superior?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Prayer at its proper time, and righteousness with the parents, and striving in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What are the most superior deeds according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates filial piety (*Birr al-Walidayn*) to the same rank as the five daily prayers and *Jihad*, highlighting its centrality in Shia jurisprudence. This triad underscores that spiritual devotion is incomplete without ethical conduct towards one's parents, a theme frequently emphasized in Shia scholarly commentaries as a prerequisite for the acceptance of worship.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘I said, ‘Which deed is the most superior?’ Heasws said: ‘The Salāt on its timing, and righteousness with the parents, and the Jihād in the Way of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Mansur ibn Hazim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Which deed is the best?’ The Imam said, ‘Prayer in its proper time, kindness to parents and hard work to strive for the cause of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’”
